title: Prox
neverSeen: Not heard in the air yet — this is the reference card.
locationOff: Turn location on — Android returns an empty scan without it and reports no error
noBle: No Bluetooth radio on this device
custom_free: Yes — the name is a free-form field in the packet. This is the only protocol here where you choose the words.
custom_fixed: No — the wording is a fixed system string chosen by a one-byte action code. The packet carries only codes and hashes.
custom_db: No — the shown name comes from a vendor database keyed by a model id, not from the advertisement.
custom_none: No — this beacon shows no text of its own.
expl_nearbyAction: Raises a setup/action sheet on nearby iPhones and iPads — 'Set Up New Device', 'Share Wi-Fi Password', Apple TV setup and so on. Which sheet appears is chosen by a one-byte action code.
expl_proximityPairing: The AirPods-style pairing card. The packet names a device model and its battery and lid state; there is no free text.
expl_nearbyInfo: Not a popup — a continuous broadcast of an iPhone's usage state (idle, active, driving). It rides alongside the action beacons and makes them fire more reliably.
expl_findMy: The Find My / offline-finding beacon a lost AirTag or device emits. Shown here for classification only; prox never transmits it.
expl_swiftPair: Pops a 'New <name> found' pairing toast on nearby Windows PCs. Its display name is a free-form string — the one place a chosen word travels in the packet.
expl_fastPair: Pops a 'Tap to pair' half-sheet on nearby Android phones. The product name and image come from Google's model database, keyed by a 24-bit id in the beacon.
expl_easySetup: Samsung's Galaxy Watch/Buds pairing sheet on a nearby Samsung phone. The shown text is Samsung's own device string, keyed by a 1-byte model id — never a name you can choose. Whether current One UI still raises it is unconfirmed.
expl_eddystone: An open beacon format from Google. Not a pairing popup; a URL frame decodes to a plain web address. Harmless and standards-defined.
labWarn: This broadcasts real pairing beacons over Bluetooth. Use it only on your own devices, in a space you control — nearby phones you do not own may show popups. At your own risk.
needsUpdate: Update the app to send — this one is older than the transmitter
profTagline: See what every phone around you is quietly broadcasting to pair
installDesc: Works offline, opens like an app
installIosHint: In Safari: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
installGenericHint: In the browser menu choose Install or Add to Home Screen.
